files.llvm/include/llvm/Transforms/Scalar/SCCP: Complete local pass API; function-scoped propagation and analysis preservation result. No additional implementation beyond reviewed SCCP.cpp.
files.llvm/include/llvm/Transforms/IPO/SCCP.h: Complete interprocedural pass API; function specialization is separately configurable and enabled by default. IPO implementation and profitability policy not reviewed by this header read.
files.llvm/include/llvm/Transforms/Utils/Predi: Complete predicate representation contract: dominated-use copies, lazy materialization only for live uses, original and renamed operands, branch/switch edge identity, assume variants, explicit owner lifetime and separate verifier/printer APIs.

insights.ink: Retain branch edge or lexical scope identity with facts; do not place a narrowed range on an expression globally. A stable scope ID can make F063 identity memo keys cheaper while preserving separation.

LLVM inserts predicate copies only when dominated uses exist. Ink can avoid expanding or keying irrelevant branch facts, but must first prove which terms depend on the predicate; simply dropping scope entries is unsound.
Distinguish original subject from a subject already refined by an outer condition. Reusing an original-node key without refined context risks losing or leaking nested facts.
LLVM assume instructions have truth semantics. Ink fallible requires/ensures may execute, fail, and return errors; do not silently replace them with assumed premises.
Function specialization can be controlled separately from fact propagation; future Ink summaries should not force cloning or code growth whenever facts improve.
Predicate map entries borrow an owner. Any query-local identity cache must keep its subjects/context alive or avoid raw identity reuse, and dispose of records with their analysis epoch.

limits: Header contracts and the already audited SCCP solver support these mappings; PredicateInfo.cpp and IPO/SCCP.cpp remain separate unreviewed implementations.
No new production predicate pass, proof rule, or performance claim.
